key: Ask whether it hurts: a placenta over the os bleeds painlessly from a soft uterus, while a separating placenta bleeds behind itself and makes the uterus painful, tender and hypertonic.
items: Painless bright red bleeding
a
The placenta over the os bleeds as the lower segment stretches, without irritating the myometrium, so there is no pain.
Soft, nontender uterus
a
Blood escapes through the cervix instead of collecting behind the placenta, so the myometrium stays relaxed.
Digital cervical exam is contraindicated
a
A finger through the os can tear a placenta lying over it and start torrential bleeding.
Placenta over the internal os on ultrasound
a
This is the definition of previa; ultrasound, including the transvaginal route, makes the diagnosis safely.
Delivery must be by cesarean
a
A placenta covering the os blocks the birth canal, so a vaginal birth would tear through it.
Fetal heart rate usually normal at first
a
The blood lost is maternal and the placenta is still attached, so fetal oxygenation holds until bleeding is heavy.
Painful bleeding with a rigid uterus
b
Blood collecting between placenta and wall irritates the myometrium, causing pain and a hypertonic, board-like uterus.
Shock out of proportion to visible blood
b
A concealed retroplacental clot can hold a large volume behind the placenta, so the blood seen underestimates the loss.
Recent cocaine use
b
Cocaine causes intense maternal vasoconstriction that can shear the placenta off the uterine wall.
Low fibrinogen and oozing IV sites
b
Tissue factor released from damaged decidua triggers DIC, which consumes fibrinogen and platelets.
Late decelerations on the fetal tracing
b
Separation removes part of the exchange surface, so the fetus becomes hypoxic during contractions.
Motor vehicle crash with abdominal trauma
b
A sudden shearing force can separate a normally implanted placenta even without visible injury to the mother.
